prebaked_qa.question: Why does heating decouple from current in an internal short?
prebaked_qa.answer:
### [Measured/Model]
In normal operational cycles, cell temperature rise is driven by external current resistive heating ($P = I^2 R$). However, during internal short circuits or exothermic decomposition, heat generation continues or accelerates even when current demand drops to zero.

### [Knowledge Base]
According to battery safety documentation [KB-01-C2], internal short circuits create localized microscopic dendritic pathways between electrodes. This triggers continuous internal chemical self-discharge through localized Joule dissipation [KB-02-C1]. Once SEI decomposition temperature (~80–120°C) is initiated, exothermic self-sustaining chemical breakdown decoupled from terminal current proceeds towards thermal runaway [KB-03-C2].
